item.title: The Andover Companies Selects Cognizant for Modernization
item.description: (Image source: The Andover Companies homepage.) The Andover Companies (Andover, Mass.) has selected Cognizant (Teaneck, N.J.) for a five-year enterprise technology modernization initiative. Cognizant will provide application and managed services for Andover’s policy administration environment, including workflow enhancements, product and pricing updates, platform upgrades and API modernization. “Our work with Andover reflects our approach to AI Builder engagements in insurance: to unlock the value of core systems and establish trusted data first, then apply AI—through platforms like Cognizant Neuro AI—carefully and responsibly, in ways that support underwriters and adjusters rather than replace their judgment.” The Andover Companies writes business through Merrimack Mutual Fire Insurance Company, Cambridge Mutual Fire Insurance Company and Bay State Insurance Company.

item.title: Powerful Quake Hits Southern Japan, Deaths Feared in Shopping Mall Blast
item.description: A 7.1-magnitude earthquake hit Japan’s southern Kumamoto prefecture on Tuesday, knocking out power to thousands of homes, rupturing roads and leaving some trapped and others presumed dead inside a partially collapsed shopping mall. Around 20 to 30 workers at the prefecture’s largest shopping mall were unaccounted for after it was rocked by an explosion in the aftermath of the quake, NHK said. “I ask everyone to take action to protect themselves, including evacuating to a safe location.” Around 300,000 people have been instructed to go to evacuation centers, and hundreds of soldiers have been deployed to help with rescue operations as aftershocks continued to rumble in the area, on Japan’s southern island of Kyushu.

item.title: Edison Rejects Blame for LA Fire Tied to Tower Idle Since 1971
item.description: Southern California Edison argued in a court filing last week that the transmission tower where last year’s deadly Eaton Fire allegedly ignited had been idle for so long, since 1971, that it no longer qualifies as the kind of public infrastructure that triggers California’s strict liability rule for utilities. In the filing, SoCal Edison and its parent company argued that the insurers’ motion should fail on several grounds, a key defense being that the idle transmission line in question was taken out of service and disconnected from the grid in 1971. Related: Edison Gets Mixed Rulings on Bid to Spread Blame for LA Wildfire The utility also argued in the filing that factual disputes remain even if its equipment is ultimately found to have sparked the fire.

item.title: Hawaii Raises Truck Bed-Riding Age to 16
item.description: But as parts of Hawaii have become more urban and roads busier and faster, especially on Oahu, where the capital city, Honolulu, is located, concern has grown about the dangers of riding in an open truck bed without seats or seatbelts. Lawmakers tried for years to put limits on the practice before passing a bill this spring that raises the minimum legal age for riding in truck beds from 12 to 16. It’s common to see people riding in the beds of pickups in Hawaii, often along country highways sandwiched between towering verdant mountains and the glassy blue expanse of the Pacific.

item.title: Diversity Crackdown Reverberates Throughout U.S. Boardrooms
item.description: President Donald Trump intensifies his campaign against diversity programs, appointments of women and racial minorities to S&P 500 boards have dropped to their lowest level in more than a decade, threatening to unwind years of gains in corporate boardroom diversity. The shift is evident in new research by recruiting firms that study leadership diversity and Reuters interviews with more than a dozen boardroom recruiters, investors and human resource analysts. It follows a series of Trump administration actions targeting diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives known as DEI.

item.title: Construction Jobsite Theft Nearly Doubled Between 2024 and 2025: Report
item.description: Jobsite thefts nearly doubled between 2024 and 2025, according to a recent joint industry report by job site security and response firms TrueLook and Noonlight. In 2025, there were 2,639 break-ins at active commercial construction sites across the U.S., nearly double the number in 2024 (1750). Peak construction season between July and December also leads to a rise in jobsite theft.

item.title: WTW launches streamlined longevity swap solution for sub-£1bn UK pension schemes
item.description: Broking group WTW has launched a new streamlined longevity swap solution called Longevity Stream, that’s set to broaden access to the expanding market for UK defined benefit schemes with £100m to £1bn of liabilities. Key features of WTW’s new longevity swap solution encompass pre-negotiated contracts, developed in collaboration with legal advisors CMS, along with a streamlined operational framework, facilitating the more efficient implementation of longevity swaps for schemes under a fixed-fee arrangement. The release of WTW’s new solution also demonstrates how the broker continues to do more work within the longevity swap market.

item.title: Cowbell introduces OMNI, an AI-native decision intelligence system for specialty insurance
item.description: Cowbell, a provider of AI-native cyber and specialty insurance solutions for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), has launched OMNI, an AI-native Decision Intelligence System designed to support the future development, underwriting, and delivery of specialty insurance products. With OMNI, we are unifying intelligence, automation, governance, and performance measurement into an AI-native Decision Intelligence System purpose-built for specialty insurance. OMNI has been developed as the intelligence layer supporting its specialty insurance operations.

item.title: KatRisk appoints Eric Robinson as Vice President of Research and Development
item.description: KatRisk, a catastrophe risk modelling company that provides analytics and insights to support the insurance and reinsurance sectors, has appointed Eric Robinson as its new Vice President of Research and Development. In his new role at KatRisk, Robinson will support the company’s research and development activities, drawing on more than a decade of experience across catastrophe modelling, insurance analytics and scientific research. Robinson joins KatRisk with extensive experience in statistical modelling, data analytics, atmospheric science and catastrophe risk modelling.

item.title: WTW introduces Longevity Stream to expand swap access for UK defined benefit schemes
item.description: WTW, a global advisory, broking and solutions company, has introduced Longevity Stream, a new longevity swap offering aimed at making longevity risk management more accessible and cost-effective for UK defined benefit pension schemes. Longevity Stream removes those barriers, giving schemes a more efficient route to market whilst retaining future flexibility and enabling them to access the attractive pricing currently available.” Amanda Chamming, Partner at CMS, added: “Longevity Stream offers great flexibility for schemes that previously may have found it difficult to access the longevity swap market, enabling them to further reduce their risk, strengthen scheme security and protect long-term outcomes for members.” Longevity Stream is intended for pension schemes with liabilities ranging from £100 million to £1 billion.

item.title: Enterprise Risk Associates Acquires Texas’ Hamann Insurance Group
item.description: Enterprise Risk Associates announced the acquisition of Hamann Insurance Group of Katy, Texas on June 17, 2026. For more than 45 years, Hamann Insurance Group has been serving both commercial and individual clients in the Houston metropolitan area. The agency has earned a reputation as a preferred insurance broker for HOAs and condominiums, and founder Dennis Hamann is a recognized leader in the specialty.

item.title: People Moves: World Insurance Names Milford Chief Broking Officer
item.description: Betsey Milord joined World Insurance Associates LLC (World), headquartered in Iselin, New Jersey, as chief broking officer. Milord will lead World’s broking organization. With more than 30 years of industry experience, Milord joins World after a decade at Marsh, where she led middle market placement operations at both the regional and national levels.

item.title: EF3 Tornado Causes Severe Damage in Northeastern Wisconsin
item.description: A tornado that caused severe damage in northeastern Wisconsin on July 27 has been preliminarily ruled as an EF3, the National Weather Service said. “If you experienced any damage, it’s important to notify your insurance agent or company right away to begin the claim process,” Wisconsin Insurance Commissioner Nathan Houdek said. The Office of the Commissioner of Insurance recommends the following tips for processing storm damage: Wisconsin has experienced an unusually active storm season.

item.title: Travelers expands product liability insurance to California life sciences companies
item.description: The post Travelers expands product liability insurance to California life sciences companies appeared first on Coverager - Insurance news and insights . Travelers announced that Travelers Synergy, its product liability insurance offering for life sciences companies, is now available in California, completing its rollout across all 50 states. Travelers Synergy is designed to protect life sciences companies against product-related claims at any point in the product development life cycle – from research and development through manufacturing and distribution.

item.title: AI and the Trusted Advisor: Growing in a Softening Market
item.description: Against that backdrop, policyholders are asking two questions more urgently than ever: “Do I need this coverage?” and if so, “How much do I need?” How brokers answer those questions is what separates a trusted advisor from a policy processor. It’s how trusted advisors scale in a faster market and how this industry keeps making the world a safer, more resilient place. As we move into Q3 2026, certain complexity trends are undeniable: stubborn inflation in sectors like construction, medical, and semiconductor costs, plus geopolitical volatility, and a growing universe of emerging risks.

item.title: Geico and Mercury: Cheapest Insurance in California
item.description: According to a recent survey by Clearsurance.com, Geico and Mercury are the cheapest home insurance providers in California . Geico writes policies nationwide, while Mercury Insurance writes policies in only a few states, specializing in California coverage. Clearsurance.com’s list of top 10 insurers in California with monthly rates is as follows: Geico – $67 Mercury – $70 AAA – $75 Traveler’s – $85 State Farm – $90 Allstate – $95 Nationwide – $100 Farmer’s – $110 Amica – $125 Chubb – $150 The premiums listed above represent what a customer would pay for $200,000 of home insurance coverage.

item.title: Apcas define sus prioridades para el segundo semestre
item.description: La Comisión Ejecutiva de Apcas analizó la pasada semana la evolución de las principales iniciativas de la asociación y estableció las prioridades para el segundo semestre del año en los ámbitos estratégico, organizativo y económico.

item.title: Allianz crea un fondo para apoyar la recuperación de las zonas afectadas por los incendios
item.description: Allianz ha anunciado la creación de un Fondo de Recuperación y Resiliencia Antiincendios con el objetivo de impulsar actuaciones dirigidas a la recuperación de las zonas afectadas por los incendios forestales y reforzar su resiliencia frente a futuros episodios.

item.title: Best AI Medical Record Summarization for Complex Claims: What Claims Teams Need
item.description: View Series For claims teams handling complex cases, including mass tort dockets, multi-provider workers’ compensation files, and IME packets running hundreds of pages, AI medical record summarization comes down to three evaluation criteria: whether the platform handles document complexity without degrading output quality, whether it provides source-linked citations reviewers can trace back to the original record, and whether human verification is built into the workflow. AI medical record summarization for complex claims teams requires a different evaluation frame than the one most vendor demos show. “Complex” in a claims context isn’t a legal category.

item.description: These are so important to the resilience of the financial system that the government granted us powers to implement a new oversight regime , and has now designated the first critical third parties (CTPs). The primary focus of our operational resilience regulatory framework has been on the ability of individual firms to prevent, respond to and recover from disruption to maintain financial stability and confidence – including from risks arising from their outsourcing and third party arrangements. Think of the last time you made a payment, transferred money, used a banking app or logged on to online financial services.

item.title: AI Seed Investors Flock To Cybersecurity
item.description: Seed funding trends tell us a lot about how savvy investors see the future unfolding. Seed investors apparently saw this coming, judging by the plethora of good-sized rounds for companies at the intersection of AI and security. Here at Crunchbase News, we took a particular interest in seed rounds in the $5 million to $10 million range, an area where cybersecurity investment was particularly robust.

item.title: Exclusive: Co-Founded By Former Whoop CTO, Throne Science Raises $10M To Track Gut Health From The Toilet
item.description: Throne Science , a startup that makes an AI-powered toilet camera to track gut health and hydration, has raised $10 million in a Series A round led by Will Ventures , it told Crunchbase News exclusively. The startup was founded in 2023 by CEO Scott Hickle , who previously worked for nearly a decade in software product management at various companies, and former Whoop co-founder and CTO John Capodilupo , for whom the company’s mission is also a bit of a personal one as he has ulcerative colitis. “We started Throne because we believe it’s inevitable that people will one day measure their health from their waste,” Hickle told Crunchbase News.

item.title: Japan struck by M6.8 earthquake in Kumamoto prefecture. Damage reported limited so far
item.description: An earthquake has struck Japan in the Kumamoto prefecture of Kyushu. However, Japan’s earthquake scale reports shaking at Shindo 7 level from this relatively shallow event, which is likely to result in some damage although reports are limited so soon after the event. The earthquake struck just south of Kumamoto city in the last hour and was at a depth of about 10 kilometers, according to the Japan Meteorological Agency.

item.title: GDP exposure to SCS events projected to rise 14% over next 30 years: First Street
item.description: Global gross domestic product (GDP) exposure to damaging severe convective storm (SCS) winds is projected to grow 14% over the next 30 years, reaching $20.2 trillion as climate risks continue to reshape underwriting globally, according to a new report by First Street, the climate risk financial modeling provider. Importantly, First Street highlighted that climate change is anticipated to accelerate exposure to damaging winds, with projections indicating increases of over 18% in the Asia-Pacific region and approximately 14% across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa within the next three decades. For the first time, cumulative insured losses from SCS events have overtaken those from tropical cyclones, First Street stated.

item.title: Secondary cat bond trading rebounds in H1 2026 as buyers outpace sellers: Swiss Re
item.description: The secondary market for catastrophe bonds remained bid-heavy during the opening half of 2026, as an influx of market participants looked to buy bonds rather than sell out of their existing positions, which caused for secondary market activity to see a meaningful increase during the period following a relatively subdued 2025, according to Swiss Re Capital Markets. In mid May, the catastrophe bond market experienced a particularly active and broad week of secondary market trading. Swiss Re Capital Markets indicated that this wave of activity highlights the increased liquidity within a maturing secondary cat bond market.

item.title: Integra and Congregational select Hadron as UK underwriting partner
item.description: UK-based MGA brands Integra Insurance Solutions and Congregational Insurance Solutions have partnered with Hadron, a multinational specialty carrier modernising the delegated authority market, to provide underwriting capacity for their respective home and church insurance programmes. Speed to market and underwriting flexibility were key considerations for Integra’s selection criteria, and Hadron’s ability to structure and deploy capacity efficiently within a clear governance framework gave both parties confidence in the long-term viability of the arrangement. Colin Johnson, International CEO of Hadron, said, “Integra has built one of the strongest home insurance platforms in the UK market, and Congregational has been serving churches and places of worship with dedication and integrity for over a century.

item.title: Oman Re’s revenue rises in H1’26 as combined ratio strengthens to 89.2%
item.description: Oman Re, the Sultanate of Oman’s sole reinsurer, has reported an increase in reinsurance revenue for the first half of 2026 to OMR 27.5 million ($71.4 million), an increase on the prior year’s OMR 26.4 million ($68.8 million), while disciplined underwriting saw the combined ratio improve year-on-year. The H1’26 combined ratio improved to 89.2% from 95.4% in H1’25, reflecting the benefits of disciplined underwriting and risk selection, said Oman Re. Additionally, as of June 30th, 2026, Oman Re’s net equity stood at OMR 45.9 million ($119.3 million), an 8% increase from December 2025 and further strengthening the capital position.

item.title: AM Best says MAPFRE’s Safety Insurance acquisition is strategically compelling
item.description: Credit rating agency AM Best has described Spain-based multinational insurance group MAPFRE S.A.’s planned acquisition of Safety Insurance Group, Inc. as strategically compelling, saying the transaction brings together two insurers with similar regional footprints and product offerings while strengthening MAPFRE’s position in Massachusetts and supporting its expansion across the New England region. Corporation (MAPFRE USA), has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Safety , a property and casualty insurer with a leading market position in Massachusetts and operations in several north-eastern US states.

item.title: Google Rivals Line Up Seeking Damages After Record $1 Billion EU Fine
item.description: A decades-long crackdown on Google’s business practices in Europe is entering a costly new phase, as the loss of the first case brought against it under new EU legislation opens the door to a wave of private lawsuits demanding up to $10 billion in damages. That has been precipitated by a $1 billion fine, the first under the Digital Markets Act, imposed on the company for favoring its own services and preventing app developers from steering users to cheaper options outside its app store Google Play. A Berlin court in November awarded Idealo €465 million ($528.9 million) in damages, the biggest fine ever awarded by a court in Germany for an antitrust infringement.

About 900,000 current and former Origin Energy Ltd. and ports operator DP World Australia , underscoring the risks to customer data and widely used services.

item.title: eBay Settles Massachusetts Couple’s Harassment, Stalking Claims for $55.7 Million
item.description: After six years of civil and criminal charges and proceedings, online shopping company eBay and several former executives will pay a total of $55.7 million to settle claims over a relentless cyberstalking and harassment campaign targeting a Massachusetts couple. In addition to $48.7 million in compensation for David and Ina Steiner of Natick, Massachusetts, the targets of the harassment, the settlement includes $6 million in charitable contributions to various nonprofit organizations, The deal also includes agreements with some individual employee defendants, a public statement by eBay, and no confidentiality restrictions. The harassment campaign by eBay employees began in 2018 after former CEO Devin Wenig criticized the Ina Steiner for her coverage of eBay and told the company’s heads of security and communications to “take her down.” They began to take steps to stop the reporting by EcommerceBytes.

item.title: NatWest partners with Uinsure
item.description: UK bank NatWest Bank has partnered with insurance broker Uinsure to launch a home insurance offering for customers and non-customers. “For a bank of NatWest’s scale to put Uinsure’s technology at the heart of its home insurance offer is a significant moment, for us and for the market. NatWest has also launched its Home Insurance Tracker through its app, allowing customers to upload and monitor the price and coverage details of an existing policy, regardless of the insurer.

item.title: Cover Genius acquires Friendsurance
item.description: Cover Genius has acquired Friendsurance, a Berlin-based provider of digital bancassurance solutions. As part of the deal, the Friendsurance team is joining Cover Genius. Together, we can offer European banking partners a clear advantage: a protection layer that is already compliant, highly optimized, and proven to drive platform yield.” – Angus McDonald, CEO and Co-founder of Cover Genius.

item.title: Builder Reciprocal writes $18.5 million in first quarter
item.description: Builder Reciprocal Insurance Exchange wrote $18.5 million in direct homeowners premium during the first quarter of 2026, with all business generated in Texas. Builder Reciprocal posted a $4.9 million underwriting loss and a $3.6 million net loss for the quarter. The Baldwin-affiliated reciprocal reported $12.5 million in direct earned premium and ceded $18.5 million in written premium during the quarter.

item.title: Chobani Fails to End Dannon Parent Danone’s Cold-Brew Coffee Suit
item.description: District Judge Jennifer Rochon in Manhattan said Dannon parent Danone DANO.PA plausibly alleged that Chobani would confuse consumers by using a yellow-and-black color scheme and the slogan “Bright & Mellow” to sell La Colombe coffee. yogurt brand Dannon for allegedly copying the packaging and slogan for a competing line of ready-to-drink cold brew coffee. Related: Danone US Sues Chobani Over High-Protein Yogurt Labeling Claims Danone uses the same colors and slogan to sell SToK coffee.

item.title: J&J to Pay $5.5 Billion to Settle Talc-Related Cancer Claims
item.description: Johnson & Johnson on Monday said it agreed to a $5.5 billion commitment to resolve years of litigation related to claims that its talc products caused ovarian cancer. The agreement requires the participation of lead plaintiff firms in ovarian talc litigation pending in state and federal courts that represent at least 95% of claims, according to J&J. The company has steadfastly maintained talc doesn’t cause cancer and that there’s never been any asbestos in its baby powder — a central claim of the lawsuits against the company.

item.title: Swiss Re appoints Benjamin Savill as CEO of Australia & New Zealand
item.description: Global reinsurer Swiss Re has appointed Benjamin (Ben) Savill as Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Australia & New Zealand, based in Sydney, effective October 1st, 2026, subject to regulatory approvals. In his new role, Savill succeeds Trent Thomson , who was appointed as the Global Head of Specialty Reinsurance at Swiss Re earlier this year. Savill has nearly three decades of industry experience across several market verticals.

item.title: Munich Re Specialty launches parametric earthquake solution through Lloyd’s Japan
item.description: Munich Re Specialty, supported by the expertise of Munich Re Capital Partners, has launched a parametric earthquake insurance solution for corporate clients in Japan, using the Lloyd’s Japan platform. Stephanie Ogden, CEO at Munich Re Specialty – Global Markets, Syndicate commented, “This parametric structured product meets a real, historic and daily challenge for businesses across Japan. Here, we enhance our purpose by enabling fast claims settlements and harnessing global collaboration, skillsets and knowledge across Munich Re.” René Mück, Global Head of Parametric NatCat at Munich Re, said, “Japan has a strong appreciation for innovative and effective risk management.

item.title: RiverStone International closes second LPT with Pacific Valley Insurance
item.description: RiverStone International, a global acquirer and reinsurer of legacy and discontinued insurance business, has signed its second loss portfolio transfer (LPT) reinsurance agreement with Pacific Valley Insurance Company. Paul Brockman, Group CEO of RiverStone International, commented: “We are delighted to have the opportunity to partner once again with Pacific Valley Insurance Company and Lyft on this transaction. Pacific Valley is a wholly owned captive insurance subsidiary of the ride sharing company Lyft.

item.title: NHTSA Rejects Petition Seeking Tesla Door-Release Defect Probe
item.description: National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has denied a petition seeking a defect investigation into the emergency mechanical door release on about 180,000 Tesla Model 3 vehicles. The petition covered about 180,000 model-year 2022 Tesla Model 3 vehicles and alleged the manual door release was difficult to locate after a crash if the vehicle lost power, increasing the risk of occupants getting trapped. NHTSA said the petition did not present evidence of a likely safety-related defect warranting an investigation and that the issue would be more appropriately addressed through an ongoing rulemaking process.

item.title: EPA Says Power for Data Centers Can Sidestep Pollution Laws
item.description: Power sources providing electricity only to data centers and not the public grid may not be subject to federal pollution laws, the U.S. The EPA said if the power plants are not supplying electricity to the grid then they would not be subject to the federal Clean Air Act’s Acid Rain Program, which has been key to the dramatic reduction of smog and soot pollution from industrial facilities. The agency said its interpretation of federal pollution laws would speed the development of artificial intelligence infrastructure while reducing strain on regional electric grids.

item.title: AI Finding Twice as Many Cyber Flaws in 2026 as It Did in 2025
item.description: The number of software security flaws discovered in popular technology products in 2026 is on pace to roughly double the tally of vulnerabilities that surfaced in 2025, an explosion driven by increasingly capable artificial intelligence systems. Internal security personnel at the technology firms are finding many of the new vulnerabilities with their own cyber-focused AI tools, according to their disclosures. The US National Vulnerabilities Database, a repository of digital security holes, recorded 45,207 flaws between January and Monday, a count approaching the total number found in all of 2025.

item.title: Vertafore Adds AI Benefits Plan Agent
item.description: The AI-powered agent is designed to automate benefit plan setup, one of the more manual workflows in benefits administration, according to a Vertafore statement. “By automating one of the most manual parts of benefits administration, we’re helping agencies create better data, move faster through critical workflows and spend more time delivering value to their clients.” The Benefit Plan Agent is built on the Vertafore Velocity AI Platform, which supports AI capabilities across Vertafore products for agencies, MGAs and carriers. (Image source: Vertafore website.) Vertafore (Denver) has launched Velocity AI Benefit Plan Agent within the BenefitPoint module of AgencyOne.

item.title: Home Trend Report: Severity Reaches All-Time High, Frequency Declines
item.description: All Peril severity reached an all-time high in 2025, rising 25.9% from a year earlier, a new report on home insurance trends shows. Home Trends Report , which looks at loss cost, claims frequency and severity. Severity reached its highest level in seven years, increasing 93.2% from 2019, offsetting lower claim frequency, the report shows.

item.title: Bill to Curb Staged Accidents Introduced in Senate
item.description: Within a reform bill out of Georgia , people involved in making claims for staged accidents would face fines of up to $100,000. The Independent Insurance Agents & Brokers of America said the federal bill would “crack down on staged accidents that endanger motorists, disrupt supply chains and fuel lawsuit abuse. The industry trades have come out to support the latest effort on Capitol Hill to thwart staged accidents.
